title: Speaker Recognition and Verification
header: Thursday 1 October 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area4 - Poster 1 - Speaker Recognition and Verification

items.title: Beyond Residual Connections: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections for Robust Speaker Representation Learning
items.authors: Zezhong Jin(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Xiaoyu Wang(Baidu); Zhe Li(Hong Kong University); Chong-Xin Gan(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Zilong Huang(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Man-Wai Mak(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Kong Aik Lee(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
items.abstract: Residual connections are fundamental to deep speaker recognition models, such as ECAPA-TDNN and ResNet. However, standard identity mapping limits information flow to a single path, constraining representation capacity. We introduce Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), reformulating residual paths as a multi-stream evolution where information is mixed through a doubly stochastic matrix. By employing Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations, mHC ensures energy conservation by preserving signal intensity and feature mean, which stabilizes gradients and mitigates signal degradation in complex networks. We evaluate mHC by replacing standard residual connections in backbones including ECAPA-TDNN, ResNet-34, Res2Net, and E-Res2Net. Extensive experiments on VoxCeleb1 demonstrate that mHC connections consistently enhances performance across all architectures, highlighting its effectiveness for robust speaker representation learning.

items.title: Mitigating Pruning-Quantization Compound Errors for Ultra-Lightweight ResNet34-Based Speaker Recognition
items.abstract: While deep neural networks (DNNs) have greatly advanced speaker recognition, backbone models such as ResNet34 still suffer from computation and memory footprints, making difficult to deploy on resource-constrained devices. To this end, we explored pruning and quantization techniques to compress speaker recognition model. Specifically, we propose a unified compression framework that combines channel pruning and low-bit quantization. Specifically, we propose ResRep-MB, a pruning strategy with multi-branch compactors for accurate channel importance assessment, achieving near-lossless structural compression. To mitigate the compound errors caused by pruning and INT4 quantization, we propose Progressive Pruning-Quantization Distillation (PPQD), which employs a dual-teacher mechanism. Experiments on VoxCeleb1 and CN-Celeb1 demonstrate that the compressed ResNet34 achieves a 19.2× compression ratio with only a 6.8% relative EER degradation, while maintaining robust cross-language performance.

items.title: Continuous 2D Spectral—Temporal Transformer for Speaker Verification
items.authors: Seongwook Ham(Soongsil University); Thien-Phuc Doan(Soongsil University)
items.abstract: Recent speaker verification (SV) systems often employ hybrid architectures that combine spectral—temporal modeling with temporal aggregation. However, approaches such as ReDimNet perform global dependency modeling after collapsing the spectral—temporal grid into a temporal representation, which removes the explicit spectral-temporal structure. We propose Continuous 2D Spectral-Temporal Transformer (C2D-ST), which maintains the spectral—temporal representation throughout the backbone and performs global dependency modeling directly on the spectral—temporal grid, with temporal-only modeling applied only in a final stage. Experiments on VoxCeleb show that C2D-ST achieves competitive performance with strong parameter efficiency, reaching 0.507 average EER with 6.9M parameters.

items.title: A Federated Learning-Based Speaker Recognition Method with Dual Classification Heads
items.authors: Ying Meng(Xinjiang University); Zhihua Fang(Xinjiang University; AGIBOT); Liang He(Xinjiang University; Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: In speaker recognition tasks, acquiring data requires significant technical and financial resources for individual organizations, while also posing risks of privacy breaches. Applying federated learning architectures can address these issues, but model performance may degrade when confronting data heterogeneity challenges. In this paper, we propose a federated learning-based speaker recognition method with dual classification heads. By introducing a more knowledgeable classification head, local models can acquire more comprehensive global knowledge, thereby improving model performance. Our method achieved an average EER improvement of 46.5% over local training and 7.6% over FedAvg when trained on the VoxCeleb2 dataset. When jointly trained on the VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb datasets, the average EER improved by 68.8% over local training and 5.4% over FedAvg.

items.title: Learning Global Key Knowledge for Federated Speaker Recognition via Fisher Information
items.authors: Ying Meng(Xinjiang University); Zhihua Fang(Xinjiang University; AGIBOT); Liang He(Xinjiang University; Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: Speaker recognition relies on substantial data to enhance model performance, but the large-scale transmission of data by individual organizations incurs privacy and economic costs. Federated learning addresses privacy concerns by avoiding direct data transmission. However, due to inconsistent client data distributions, local models may learn redundant knowledge, leading to degraded performance. In this work, we utilise the Fisher Information Matrix to extract key dimensions from embeddings, enabling representation alignment between global and local models. By instructing local models to learn critical knowledge from the global model, we mitigate the detrimental effects of redundant knowledge, thereby enhancing overall model performance.

items.title: HistoMatch: Unified Transient-Steady Assessment for Noise-Robust Semi-Supervised Speaker Verification
items.authors: Shenghan Gao(UCAS; IOA); Xueshuai Zhang(IOA); Pengyuan Zhang(UCAS; IOA); Yonghong Yan(UCAS; IOA)
items.abstract: Speaker verification systems have gained widespread applications across various domains, benefiting from advances in deep learning. However, acquiring large-scale labeled data remains challenging, making semi-supervised learning with pseudo-labeling a critical research focus. Current pseudo-labeling approaches predominantly rely on confidence thresholds-a transient metric vulnerable to distortions induced by random segmentation and noise augmentation. To overcome this limitation, we propose HistoMatch, a novel mechanism that leverages historical prediction stability as a steady-state metric. Combined with transient confidence, it forms a Dual-state History-based Stability Evaluator (DHSE) for high-quality unlabeled data selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our semi-supervised approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on all three VoxCeleb1 test sets, with remarkable equal error rates (EER) of 0.91%, 1.13%, and 2.13%-closely approaching fully supervised benchmarks.

items.title: Self-supervised Speaker Verification with High-Confidence Pseudo-Label Selection and DINO-Style Self-Distillation Based on Pre-trained Models
items.authors: Yishuang Li(Malanshan audio & video Lab); Yi Yu(Malanshan audio & video Lab); Wanli Dong(Malanshan audio & video Lab); Weihao Gan(Malanshan audio & video Lab)
items.abstract: In this paper, we propose a self-supervised speaker verification (SS-SV) method based on pre-trained models (PTMs), which improves performance via high-confidence pseudo-label selection and DINO-style self-distillation. We select the top-K most speaker-discriminative Transformer layers from PTMs and cluster their representations separately to generate multiple pseudo-label sets. Using label alignment, we retain samples with consistent clustering as high-confidence pseudo-labeled data, while others are treated as unlabeled. We perform pseudo-supervised learning with label noise correction loss on the high-confidence set;for unlabeled data we use an EMA teacher to provide soft distillation targets and apply a consistency loss for regularization. These objectives are jointly optimized to train the SV model. Experiments on the VoxCeleb dataset show that our SS-SV method achieves performance comparable to current state-of-the-art approaches, demonstrating its effectiveness.

items.title: Stabilizing Short Duration Speaker Verification through Neural Re-scoring with Hybrid Enrollment
items.authors: Zhiqi Ai(Shanghai University); Cheng Han(Shanghai University); Shiyi Mu(Shanghai University); Zhiyong Chen(Hithink RoyalFlush AI Research Institute); Yongjin Zhou(Shanghai University); Shugong Xu(Xi’an Jiaotong Liverpool University)
items.abstract: Short-duration speaker verification (SDSV) is crucial for personalized keyword spotting, where test utterances are typically shorter than three seconds. Limited speech duration results in unstable speaker representations and increased sensitivity to noise and phoneme variations, thereby degrading performance. To investigate this issue, we construct VoxPhrase, a large-scale SDSV corpus automatically segmented from the VoxCeleb dataset. Our analysis shows that text-dependent (TD) enrollment is constrained by duration and yields unstable speaker representations. In contrast, although text-independent (TI) enrollment introduces content mismatch, its representations become more stable as the enrollment duration increases. Accordingly, we propose a hybrid-enrollment neural re-scoring framework that combines TD and TI enrollment and performs frame-level comparison via parallel cross-attention. Experiments on VoxPhrase demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple speaker models.

items.title: VieSpeaker: A Large-Scale Vietnamese Speaker Recognition Dataset Beyond Visual Dependency
items.authors: Viet Hoang Pham(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Tran Trung Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Bao Thu Ho(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Phuong Tuan Dat(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Thi Thu Trang Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Speaker recognition has advanced rapidly with large-scale training datasets, yet Vietnamese remains under-resourced, with existing corpora limited in scale and acoustic diversity. Most large-scale datasets rely on facial cues to link speech with speaker identities, restricting data collection to recordings where speakers appear on camera. We propose a face-independent dataset construction pipeline and introduce VieSpeaker, a large-scale Vietnamese speaker recognition dataset. Our approach leverages textual metadata and large language model reasoning to infer speaker identities from transcripts and contextual information. VieSpeaker contains approximately 902 hours of speech from 4,715 speakers. Experiments show that models trained on VieSpeaker achieve improved robustness and generalization compared to existing Vietnamese datasets. This work demonstrates the feasibility of face-independent dataset construction and provides a new direction for building large-scale speech resources.

items.title: Confusion-Transport Pruning: Optimal-Transport Redundancy and CKA Geometry Distillation for Hard-Set Robust Speaker Verification
Function words: a topic independent approach to word n-gram selection for forensic speaker comparison
items.abstract: This paper highlights an issue with likelihood ratio-based forensic speaker comparison (LR-based FSC) systems that exploit speaker idiosyncrasies in word choice. A baseline experiment using word n-gram features from speech transcripts of 104 Australian male speakers achieves a Cllr of 0.60. However, it is shown that topic dependent terms are included in the feature set, which may bias the result. In turn, this may lead to an overestimation of the strength of evidence obtainable from word n-gram based features. A simple but novel approach to circumventing this problem using function words is presented and evaluated. An explicitly defined features set of 156 function words is shown to yield a Cllr of 0.83. Subsequent evaluation of five filter based feature selection methods applied to the set demonstrates an notable improvement in performance when using the ANOVA F-ratio procedure (Cllr = 0.78). This result is coupled with a substantial reduction in dimension size to k= 50 features.

items.title: Codec-induced Mismatch, Speech Duration, and Speaker-dependent Effect in a DNN-based Forensic Speaker Recognition System
items.authors: Guangmou Deng(Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Bruce Xiao Wang(Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Vincent Hughes(University of York)
items.abstract: The performance of forensic automatic speaker recognition (FASR) systems under the combined effects of codec-induced mismatch and different questioned-speech (QS) durations remains insufficiently understood, particularly at the individual speaker level. This study investigates the combined impact of representative lossy speech codecs (G.711 A-law, AMR-NB, and Opus) and QS duration on a DNN (ResNet34-MHA)-based FASR system. System-level performance was generally good across all codec conditions, especially with >30s speech. Codec effects vary, however, with low-bitrate AMR-NB causing the greatest degradation in performance and Opus having minimal impact. Crucially, individual-level analyses reveal substantial speaker-dependent variability that is obscured by system-level metrics: some speakers exhibit persistently poor or unstable performance, and speakers with poorer overall performance are more sensitive to codec-induced mismatch. These findings demonstrate that promising system-level performance does not guarantee good performance for all speakers and highlights the need for individual-level analysis when testing DNN-based FASR systems.
